Are you aspiring to become a real estate agent and don’t know where to start? Well, you’ve come to the right place. The first big decision you’ll make is deciding where you’ll complete your licensing education. Finding the right program will give you the confidence and tools to pass the exam and hit the ground running.

There are so many online real estate schools that claim to be the best, but it’s not easy to know which programs are really worth it. That’s where we come in. We’ve reviewed the best online real estate schools based on what future real estate agents really care about – flexibility, pricing, pass rates and student support. Let’s take a look at your options to see which one is the right fit for you.

Before you review the school information below, here are the features you should pay attention to when deciding on which online real estate school is best for you.

Now that you’re armed with a checklist of items to keep your eye on, continue reading to choose the best school for your needs.

The CE Shop offers real estate courses in all 50 states, plus the District of Columbia, and boasts a 96% student satisfaction rate. Students attribute this to its engaging course features, student support and a proprietary online learning platform called LEAP.

You can complete your online real estate prelicensing coursework in as little as two weeks if your schedule permits. The CE Shop regularly updates course content, and every topic covered is based on commonly faced, real-life scenarios. It can be tough to stay consistent with self-paced courses, but The CE Shop makes it easier with interactive content with built-in progress tracking to keep you engaged and motivated.

If you’re concerned about investing in a course you’re not sure will be a good fit for you, The CE Shop offers a free five-day trial with unlimited access for all prelicensing courses. What’s more, they offer a money-back guarantee within 30 days of purchase, as long as your course is less than 50% complete.

The CE Shop’s product offerings include prelicensing, post-licensing, continuing education and exam prep courses, depending on your state. In most states, The CE Shop offers exam prep and continuing education courses that can be bundled with prelicensing courses for convenience and significant savings. As an added bonus, they offer a pass guarantee with any Exam Prep Edge purchase for prelicensing. If you don’t pass, they will refund the cost of your initial licensing exam.

The CE Shop’s courses can be accessed through your tablet, computer or smartphone 24/7 for on-the-go learning that is flexible and convenient. On the downside, the course can be heavy on text and light on video lessons. With certain packages, you get unlimited attempts at passing the course’s final exam.

Colibri offers real estate courses in 40 states plus Washington, D.C. More than 1.5 million students have enrolled in Colibri Real Estate’s courses to complete their education requirements and prepare for the license exam, and students give the school a rating of 4.5 out of 5 stars.

Prelicensing course upgrades include Exam Prep Plus for instructor engagement and study tools, and Ultimate Learning for access to the school’s Career Booster. If you’re balancing completing your education requirements with work and family demands, you’ll appreciate being able to move through the online course at your own pace with the next-generation student dashboard.

Students enjoy Colibri’s clear course format, real-world examples and practice exams that simulate live tests and include assessments. Colibri offers a Pass or Don’t Pay Guarantee. If you don’t pass the licensing exam within 30 days of completing your course, Colibri will reimburse the cost of the purchased package, unless state laws or regulations prohibit qualification for the guarantee.

Colibri’s product offering includes post-licensing courses, exam prep and continuing education courses in most states listed above, in addition to prelicensing courses. They also offera pass or don’t pay guarantee.

Colibri’s self-paced and livestream courses are designed to allow you to study on any device with internet access and a browser, including your smartphone or tablet. With 24/7 access to the dashboard, you can stop and start your course anytime without losing track of your progress.

While it doesn’t operate in all 50 states, Aceable Agents offers prelicensing courses in 15 states, including Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Michigan, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia and Washington.

Built by learning science experts, Aceable Agent’s workshops, practice tests and other study tools are designed to help you pass your exam on the first try. The school offers a first-of-its-kind mobile app from which students can complete their studies, anytime from any device.

The hands-free audio narration lets you tune in as you would to your favorite podcast. We also love the Mastery Tracking algorithm. As you progress through your course, it learns where you need improvement and provides personalized exam prep. Students can switch between their browser and Aceable Agent’s mobile app, both of which track and save progress, so you can stop and resume your studies when it’s convenient for you across devices.

Aceable Agent is so confident that you’ll love their courses, they offer a 30-day money-back guarantee. If you did not complete the course and don’t feel their program is right for you – you can request a full refund. The school also has an Ace or Don’t Pay Guarantee, so students who take one of AceableAgent’s prelicensing courses and don’t pass the licensing exam are eligible for a refund.

AceableAgent’s product offering includes post-licensing courses, exam prep and continuing education courses in most states, in addition to prelicensing courses. Course availability varies by state, so be sure to check if the course you are looking for is available in your area.

Students have access to self-paced, online courses from a mobile device or computer at any time of day. Aceable Agent’s courses feature interactive games, videos and bite-sized lessons to help students successfully meet prelicensing coursework requirements and pass the state and national exams. While most students appreciate that course content is presented in a highly engaging way to help with retention, interactive courses may not be best for visual learners who prefer to read or see pictures.

Kaplan offers real estate pre-licensing courses in 33 states including Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington and Wisconsin.

While Kaplan does not publish pass rates, the school is committed to your success. They offer the Kaplan Commitment which promises that they will continue to support your studies for the same state exam at no cost to you. With over 50 years of experience, Kaplan has helped thousands of students begin and advance their real estate careers every year.

Kaplan’s real estate course uses interactive content that combines industry fundamentals with the latest state-specific information needed to pass your state’s licensing exam. Video-based courses make complex topics easier to understand and feel more like a real classroom experience. Even better, the courses are created by real estate experts to mirror licensing exam topics to give you a greater chance to pass the exam on your first try.

Kaplan’s self-paced, online prelicensing offerings let you start, stop and resume your course when it’s convenient for you. In addition to prelicensing courses, the school offers continuing education packages and exam prep courses in most states. Full tuition refunds are available within 30 days of purchase for web-based courses and online classes that have not been completed.

Kaplan’s product offering includes prelicensing courses in over 30 states, post-licensing courses, exam prep and continuing education courses in many of those states. Exam prep is included in most packages and backed by some of the best educators in the business.

You can access your courses online and the courses are mobile-friendly. Access your courses anywhere, anytime from your laptop, tablet or mobile device. Kaplan’s online video courses complement text-based course content to reinforce key concepts, even on the go.

To find the best online real estate school, we have evaluated dozens of real estate schools, reviewing both online and in-person programs. We’ve chosen schools with interactive content, hands-free audio, mobile learning and other convenient formats that will help you fit your studies into your busy schedule. Our real estate experts possess in-depth knowledge of real estate licensing and online courses and evaluate real estate licensing programs based on pricing, course packages, course materials, teaching styles, online user experience, exam success rates, customer reviews and more.

The best online real estate schools on our list are not only widely available — they offer economies of scale that make their course packages affordable — using tech that makes their online courses way more convenient than having to commute to attend in-person classes at a brick-and-mortar location. Unlike your local school, they have the scale to invest in leading-edge technology that makes getting prepped for your state real estate exam a snap.

Don’t believe us? Check out our real estate education page for more information about getting licensed and the best real estate schools available in your state. We recommend the schools on this list for their convenience, value for money, excellence in course materials and thoughtful user experience.

Each state has its own license reciprocity and portability rules, and many have license reciprocity agreements with other states. If you have your real estate license in one state and want to conduct business in another, check with the state you are not licensed in to see if they will waive your prelicensing education requirements based on a license reciprocity agreement.

The schools featured in this guide make it easy to sign up for your online real estate classes. Just click the website of the school of your choice below, select the package you want from the school’s catalog, add it to your cart, check out and wait for the school to deliver your course (typically as a link, email, or both).

In-person real estate classes can be beneficial if you prefer a traditional learning atmosphere and have an incredibly flexible schedule. But for anyone pursuing a real estate license who has to juggle a full-time job, family, and other obligations, a school offering 100% online real estate classes is a much more convenient option.

Now that you know what the industry-leading online real estate schools have to offer, you can make the most informed decision to launch a new career. Once you have obtained your license, you’ll be ready to complete any post-licensing requirements, continuing education requirements, or pursue your broker’s license. #5369. SAP reportedly plans to lay off 10,000+ employees amid AI push

Enterprise software giant SAP SE is reportedly planning to lay off at least 10,000 employees, or more than 9% of its workforce.

Bloomberg today cited sources as saying that the scope of the restructuring initiative is still subject to change.

According to the publication, SAP and a labor council in its home country of Germany have negotiated an “employment guarantee” that will run through 2028. That may mean the layoffs will mainly affect employees in other markets. The report indicates that SAP’s product, engineering and sales units are expected to see the largest cuts.

Executives have reportedly also asked other departments to find cost reduction opportunities.

The reported restructuring push follows a banner quarter for SAP. The company’s sales and adjusted profit both topped analyst expectations. Its €24.11 billion cloud contract backlog, a measure of future revenue, also came in ahead of the consensus estimate.

The planned layoffs are said to be connected to SAP’s efforts to integrate more artificial intelligence features into its products. The company is best known for its ERP, or enterprise resource planning, software. Enterprises use it to automate a long list of backoffice tasks and share data between teams. SAP also sells cloud services for other use cases such as sales automation and customer support.

At a May user conference, the company introduced an AI interface called Joule Work for its applications. SAP says that the tool will enable workers to centrally access its products instead of navigating multiple screens.

Joule Work made its debut alongside a suite of AI agents dubbed Joule Assistants. According to SAP, they will use over 200 subagents to automate repetitive business tasks. Another new offering, Industry AI, will automate sector-specific workflows.

The report that SAP is preparing for job cuts doesn’t come as a complete surprise. Last week, Chief Financial Officer Dominik Asam told attendees of an investor event that the company expects its headcount to decline. Additionally, two of the software maker’s six directors will reportedly leave in connection with its shift to a more AI-centric strategy.

It’s unclear when the job cuts will take place. According to Bloomberg, SAP historically announced workforce reduction programs in January. The software maker took that route with its last major restructuring initiative, which saw it axe about 10,000 roles in 2024. The initiative cost about €3 billion.

The company said in a statement that “SAP continuously reviews its organization to ensure it remains aligned with its strategy and customer needs.”

#5368. 8 best Florida real estate schools for 2026

Our editors independently review the products we recommend. When you buy through our links, we may earn a commission. Learn more

Are you ready to begin a fulfilling real estate career in the Sunshine State? To get started, you have to complete 63 hours of prelicensing coursework through a state-approved real estate school before you’re allowed to take the licensing exam. Most schools offer this online now, which makes it easier to work through the material without putting your life on hold.

Not all online Florida real estate schools are the same. Some are better if you want structure and support while others work well if you just want to get through the coursework at your own pace. We’ve broken down the best online Florida real estate schools for 2026, comparing course formats, pricing, study tools and exam prep so you can choose the option that actually fits how you learn and fits your budget.

The CE Shop earns our top spot for one simple reason – it combines strong course content with tools that actually help students pass the exam. Features like a five-day free trial, a pass guarantee and its Exam Prep Edge study tools are all included with higher-tier packages, making it easier to prepare without having to guess what you’ll need to pass the exam.

Their platform is easy to use and includes short, self-paced lessons that allow you to fit lessons into your busy schedule without losing your place. Exam Prep Edge includes quizzes, flashcards, matching exercises and practice tests that reinforce key concepts as you go. For students thinking beyond licensing, the Premium Package also includes first-time renewal coursework and access to the Kickstarter Professional Development Program, which covers business planning, lead generation and negotiation basics.

The CE Shop offers four prelicensing course packages, plus Florida real estate continuing education and broker licensing courses in Florida. All three top-tier prelicensing packages include Exam Prep Edge to help you retain information and ace the exam.

Aceable Agent takes an innovative approach to online learning, with classes offered through its website, unique mobile app and podcast-style audio courses. Its self-paced and cost-effective Florida real estate courses help you learn on the go, so your study schedule can fit your busy life. Courses include engaging videos, interactive games, infographics and knowledge checks that use straightforward language and real-life scenarios inside bite-sized lessons to keep you engaged with the material.

Designed by learning science experts using proven instructional principles, Aceable Agent’s easy-to-understand courses have frequent practice tests, so you’ll go into the state exam feeling confident. Mastery Tracking helps you focus your energy on your weakest areas when studying for your course final and state licensing exams.

Aceable Agent offers three self-paced prelicensing course packages that include audio and video lessons and practice questions. Their Deluxe and Premium packages incorporate additional features like instructor support, exam prep, AI tools and live webinars.

Colibri Real Estate is a great option for students who want structure and help staying on track to meet their learning goals. With hundreds of thousands of agents trained by Colibri, their focus is on providing structured coursework with support from local real estate experts. The online platform is built around accountability by tracking your study time, setting weekly goals and clearly showing your progress, which can be helpful if you do better with defined milestones.

Colibri offers courses with interactive lessons and practice exams designed to reinforce key concepts as you move through the material. The courses also offer exam prep options, even in the lower-priced packages. The standard package includes practice tests and live Q&A sessions. Higher-tier packages include CompuCram Exam Prep with flashcards, audio reviews, readiness assessments and simulated exams. The Ultimate Learning package includes career resources such as how-to videos, checklists and a customizable business plan.

Colibri Real Estate offers four Florida prelicensing course packages, along with options for continuing education and broker licensing. Higher-tier packages include additional exam prep tools and study resources.

Casa Academy is an innovative real estate school in Florida that focuses on audio and AI to make learning easy. While they do offer self-paced courses from your laptop, Casa also has all of their course available on Spotify so you can learn on the go. Each class is structured as an informative discussion, so you’ll get real-world knowledge from experts that you will apply to your future career.

In addition, the integrated AI, built with ChatGPT, is there to enhance your educational experience. The AI tutor remembers your weaknesses and helps you review them until they become strengths. It will prompt you with explanations, quick reviews and drills to keep your knowledge sharp so you’re ready to pass the real estate exam.

Casa Academy provides basic packages with all the course hours you need:

Kaplan Real Estate Education has several packages to help students get ready for the Florida licensing exam. The courses are structured and detailed, with clear explanations that make it easier to understand some of the tougher concepts that Florida requires to pass the exam. Students like having different ways to study, whether that’s watching an instructor online, working through printed materials or using practice tests to see where they stand.

Kaplan’s exam prep tools and student support are what set this school apart. The study guide is detailed, and the practice questions are worded the same way you’ll see them on the exam. If you want a course that keeps you focused and gives you plenty of practice before exam day, Kaplan should be at the top of your list. Even though it comes with a higher price tag, the detailed content is well worth the investment.

Gold Coast Schools is a good option for students who want live instruction and a more hands-on learning experience. While its online courses are powered by Colibri’s learning platform, Gold Coast operates as its own Florida-based school with a strong focus on instructor access and student support.

Although the school doesn’t offer a mobile app, it does stand out for its personalized guidance. Students can speak directly with career counselors when deciding which course to take. Gold Coast also offers classroom, livestream and online options, with courses available in both English and Spanish.

In addition to prelicensing, Gold Coast offers post-licensing, continuing education and broker licensing education. Prelicensing education is offered in three different packages outlined below.

RealEstateU offers a straightforward, courses-only package that saves you money. If you feel confident taking exams and preparing for them, this low-cost real estate course may be right for you. If not, RealEstateU also offers two premium course bundles that go beyond just passing the real estate exam. They provide real-world strategies for success in your new career, like negotiation strategies, how to convert leads and how to choose the right brokerage. You’ll also learn the business of practicing real estate, including expenses, earning potential, commission structures and more.

RealEstateU’s exam study guide is included in their two top-tier packages. It offers practice questions and four practice exams to test your knowledge. If you prefer, audio lessons are available or you can download lessons and study materials to access them offline – providing flexibility if you can’t access wifi or the internet.

RealEstateU’s Florida prelicensing course starts at $99, making it the most affordable option on our list. Exam prep and additional study resources may cost extra, so make sure you factor that into your total budget if you need extra support.

VanEd stands out for how clear it is about what students are signing up for. You get a five-day free trial with full course access, which makes it easier to decide if the format works for you before committing. VanEd has been developing real estate courses for more than 17 years, with content built by instructors who understand both the licensing process and what Florida students need to know to pass the exam.

The courses use a mix of videos, infographics, flashcards and interactive exercises to keep the material moving. VanEd also includes virtual field trips that connect concepts to real-world scenarios, which can help with retaining what you learn. Everything works across all devices, so you can study from your laptop, tablet or phone and pick up where you left off.

VanEd offers three course packages at an affordable price. The five-day free trial is included in every package.

To determine the very best Florida real estate schools, we conducted extensive research, rating each school based on the following:

Finally, we considered the schools with unique features and professional development opportunities that can have significant value for real estate agents. We do the research so you don’t have to, bringing it all together in this guide to the best real estate schools in Florida. All that’s left for you to do is choose one and launch your new career.

The cost to get your real estate license in Florida depends mostly on the school and course package you choose. The biggest expense is the required 63-hour prelicensing course, which can range from lower-cost, self-paced options to more expensive packages that include exam prep, instructor access, or career resources. On top of that, Florida charges separate fees for the license application and the state exam.

When you add everything up, most people can expect to spend somewhere between $180 and $600 to get licensed. If you stick with a basic course, you’ll be closer to the lower end – and vice versa.

How long it takes to become a Florida real estate agent depends on how quickly you complete the required steps. The state requires 63 hours of prelicensing coursework, which some people finish in a few weeks if they move quickly, while others take a couple of months studying part-time. Once you complete the course, you’ll need to pass the state exam and submit your license application.

For most people, the process can take anywhere from one to three months. It depends on whether you’re studying full-time or part-time and what other commitments you may be juggling at the same time.

Once you have passed the real estate licensing exam, you can apply for a Florida real estate sales associate license online. In fact, Florida prioritizes flexibility, allowing licensees to take the prelicensing course, submit their license application and even take the state exam online through Pearson VUE proctoring.

The Florida Real Estate License Exam tends to be one of the more difficult to pass. There are 100 multiple-choice questions on the Florida real estate licensing exam, and the required passing score is 75%. According to the data available on Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR), as well as other reputable digital resources and news sites, there is a 40-50% pass rate for those taking the Florida real estate exam for the first time. This makes it all the more important to make sure you choose the best real estate school to help you pass the exam on the first try.

According to Indeed, the average Florida real estate agent earns $101,676 annually (as of this writing), which is actually the same as the national average.

Getting your real estate license in Florida starts with choosing the right school helping you feel prepared on exam day and beyond. Some people need structure and guidance. Others just want a straightforward way to finish the coursework and move on. The schools in this guide give you options either way.

Our goal is to make the comparison easier by laying out what each school actually offers, so you can choose a course that fits your schedule, budget and learning style. #5367. Tech Moves: Microsoft names 2 leaders, loses 1; DoorDash VP departs; BluePill, Glacis get execs

Tech Moves covers notable hires, promotions and personnel changes in the Pacific NW tech community. Submissions: [email protected]

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 18, 2026 at 12:47 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 11:47 am

— Weiwei Yang has left Microsoft after more than a decade to co-found a startup that is “building the power grid for the AI age,” according to her LinkedIn profile.

Yang was most recently a senior director with Microsoft Research, working on grid technology. Her team built a grid dataset and released small foundation models to help users operate and expand electrical infrastructure.

Yang thanked her community at the tech giant, adding, “I hope the relationships and collaborations we’ve built continue well beyond Microsoft, and that we find many new ways to work together.”

— Allie Mellen has joined Microsoft as principal director for security research and threat intelligence. Mellen was previously a principal analyst at Forrester. She also wrote “Code War,” a book that explores cyberattacks as a powerful geopolitical weapon.

In her new role, Mellen said she will lead strategy for protection and threat intelligence, “helping shape what intelligence we produce, how AI can improve its speed and quality, and how we turn that knowledge into better protection for customers.”

— Agility Robotics, the Salem, Ore., company that had its Nasdaq debut earlier this month, has announced three leadership changes:

— Former tech executive Drew Sheriff has been named CEO and president of the Space Needle and Chihuly Garden and Glass. Sheriff was previously a vice president at DoorDash and has held leadership roles at Amazon, Starbucks and Parachute Home. His roles focused on customer experience, product growth, strategy and marketing.

“His skill set is the ideal background for charting how we attract customers and how we delight customers in this new age,” Jeff Seely, board chair for the Space Needle and Chihuly Garden and Glass, told the Seattle Times.

— Microsoft has named Caroline King as director of its Washington state community and philanthropy team, with a focus on advocacy work across housing, affordability and other priority issues.

King is the founder and past CEO of Washington STEM, an organization that coordinates research, advocacy, policy, philanthropy and partnerships to support science, technology, engineering and math education in the state. She most recently served as a leader on the governing body of an international school in Luxembourg.

— Longtime Amazon and Microsoft tech exec Scott Wiltamuth has retired — mostly.

Wiltamuth joined Amazon in 2011 as an AWS vice president overseeing a large organization building developer and management tools. In 2018, he took a seven-month leave for colon cancer treatment. After returning, he sought a director-level position and thanked company leaders for helping him find a better fit. “Their flexibility and creativity enabled me to extend my AWS career,” he said.

Wiltamuth launched his tech career at Microsoft in 1993 and left nearly 19 years later as director of program management for Visual Studio Pro.

He now spends time with his wife and family, traveling, golfing, swimming and reading. “I don’t plan to pursue another full-time operational role,” Wiltamuth said, “but may do some part-time work.”

— Adam Nygate has exited Palo Alto Networks to co-found and lead a stealth startup based in Seattle. He was founder and CEO of Huntr, a platform launched in 2019 where security researchers could submit information on AI and machine learning vulnerabilities. Protect AI acquired Huntr, and Palo Alto Networks later acquired Protect AI.

“Huntr was a bet that open source gets safer when vulnerabilities are visible to the people who can fix them, even when that made life uncomfortable for vendors who’d rather keep things quiet,” Nygate said in a post announcing his career change and impending new baby.

— BluePill, a Seattle-based marketing startup that helps brands predict consumer behavior, has named Mike Weis as chief revenue officer and head of sales.

Weis has 40 years of experience in consumer packaged goods, retail and commerce, beginning his career as a Pacific Northwest leader at Unilever and holding executive positions at Catalina and Quotient Technologies. Recent roles include adviser at Contento2, eGateway Capital and And1 Advisors.

“Beyond the incredible résumé, Mike is one of the kindest, most genuine, and most passionate people I’ve met. Someone who has accomplished so much, yet brings so much humility, curiosity, and energy to every conversation,” said Ankit Dhawan, CEO and founder of BluePill.

— Glacis, a Seattle startup that builds tamper-proof records of AI behavior, has named Caer Mistral Sanders as a technical co-founder. Sanders has launched startups and joins Glacis from Thoughtworks. Before that, she held leadership roles at Wayfair and Onshape. As a teenager, she published a book on mixed-reality control systems and won a world robotics championship.

In a post announcing the new role, Sanders said she has designed medical record systems, researched robot communication, patented cryptographic technology and built widely used AI platforms. “This is the first time in my career I get to bring all of those skills to bear on one problem, and I couldn’t be more excited!” she added.

— The PNW Battery Collaborative has welcomed Jason Demeny as its director of communications. Demeny is a marketing leader whose past employers include Crusoe, Patch, Qualtrics and Apptio. Earlier in his career, he spent more than a decade at Microsoft over two stints, most recently leading teams that served the Azure Partner Experience group.

The nonprofit PNW Battery Collaborative brings together startups, innovators and researchers focused on energy storage.

— Tom Wheeler, former chairman of the Federal Communications Commission, has joined the advisory council for Known, a Bellevue, Wash.-based company building accountability infrastructure for autonomous AI. Wheeler led the FCC from 2013 to 2017.

Known, previously called Identity Digital Innovation Labs, spun out of Identity Digital in September.

— Versium has promoted Matthew Baumgartner to vice president of engineering. The Redmond, Wash.-based company provides data and software that help businesses identify potential customers, fill in missing contact information and target their marketing. Baumgartner has been with Versium since 2018.

— Charlie Trillingham has been named communications manager for the University of Washington AI and Machine Learning for Engineering programs and the UW NSF AI Institute for Dynamic Systems. He previously served as a marketing and communications lead for the Buerk Center for Entrepreneurship within the UW’s Foster School of Business.

Editor’s note: Story updated 11/19 to correct that Charlie Trillingham worked for the Buerk Center for Entrepreneurship within the UW’s Foster School of Business, not the Foster School itself.

#5365. ‘Sister isn’t free’: Melinda French Gates fact-checks viral ‘SNL’ sketch on eldercare

Geek Life: Fun stories, memes, humor and other random items at the intersection of tech, science, business and culture.  SEE MORE

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 1:23 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 1:23 pm

A “Saturday Night Live” skit about caring for aging relatives touched a viral nerve after it aired over the weekend, including with Melinda French Gates, who offered her own “fact check” on the too-close-to-home comedy.

The sketch, a fake commercial, stars host John Mulaney as a man who has found an easy way to care for his aging father without upending his own life: “Sister,” an “elder care system” that is free and is, in fact, his sister.

French Gates wrote on Instagram this week that the sketch “is funny because it’s a little too true.” Using research from Pivotal, her investment and philanthropic organization, she went through the ad’s claims one by one and found that most held up:

Sister will provide. True, French Gates said, citing AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Among adults ages 55 to 64, women are nearly 40% more likely than men to care for an older relative, and nearly 40% more likely to provide constant care.

She’ll quit her job. “Mostly true,” at least the job part. Catalyst found that 42% of women who voluntarily left jobs in 2025 cited caregiving as the main reason.

Paid help is pricey. “True, unfortunately.” New America puts the average home health aide at more than $6,600 a month, and 24-hour care can top $25,000.

Sister may break down. Also true. In the Caregiving in the U.S. 2025 report, nearly two-thirds of caregivers said they were under moderate or high emotional stress, and women felt the strain more than men did.

“Free” is misleading. French Gates said Sister isn’t free; she’s the one paying for the care, in lost wages, stalled careers, thinner retirement savings and less time for her own life.

French Gates has made women’s health and caregiving central to her work since she stepped down as co-chair of the Gates Foundation in 2024.

She left with $12.5 billion to put toward her work on behalf of women and families. Much of that work runs through Pivotal, the Seattle-area organization she founded to handle her philanthropy and investments. In June she pledged another $215 million for women’s health, which brought her giving in that area to more than $600 million over two years. The pledge included $10 million to the Menopause Society for better menopause care in the U.S.

The sketch has been shared widely across the country this week, in part because it lines up so closely with the research.

In its own analysis, The New York Times cited studies showing that daughters generally provide at least twice as much care to aging parents as sons do. The U.S., unlike many wealthy countries, offers no federal paid leave or long-term care insurance for family caregivers.

French Gates said she welcomed the conversation.

“I’m so glad we’re talking about this, and laughing about it,” she wrote on Instagram. “We need more honesty about what caring for loved ones really takes and why so much of that work falls to women. But I’d love for the day to come when these jokes don’t pack quite the same punch — because we’ve made it so much easier to care for the people we love.”

#5363. Google acquires Seattle startup Howie and its AI scheduling assistant

Chronicling the Seattle and Pacific Northwest startup scene. SEE MORE

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 18, 2026 at 2:03 pmNovember 18, 2026 at 2:03 pm

Google is bringing Seattle-based Howie, maker of an AI scheduling assistant that works from your inbox, into its Google Labs division.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed this week. Google Labs, the company’s experimental arm, announced the acquisition in a post on X, saying it “can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses.”

Howie CEO and co-founder Austin Petersmith said on LinkedIn that the team will continue building Howie at Google. “Howie has always been built on top of Gmail and Google Calendar, so Google Labs is the perfect place for us to take this product to the next level,” he wrote.

Petersmith co-founded Howie around 2023 with CTO Dave Newman. The two first worked together in 2013 at Assembly, which Newman co-founded, and prototyped an AI assistant in 2015 before deciding the market wasn’t ready.

We’re excited to welcome Howie to Google Labs! The @Howie_ai team has spent years figuring out scheduling and calendar management. We can’t wait to learn from them as we build the next generation of intuitive AI tools together for small businesses 🤝 https://t.co/8bzjebeGdD

Users cc Howie on an email thread, and it coordinates meeting times, adds events to calendars, follows up as needed and flags scheduling conflicts. Customers set their own rules in an open-ended preferences document, such as “if it’s a pitch call, set it to 25 minutes and use Zoom.”

Behind the scenes, Howie ran tasks through fine-tuned language models and looped in human scheduling experts when the AI wasn’t confident.

Howie raised a $6 million seed round led by True Ventures in September 2025, when it launched publicly out of private beta. At the time, it had more than 1,000 paying customers, including startup founders, venture capitalists, recruiters, consultants and journalists, and was scheduling more than 5,000 meetings a week.

The deal comes as Google and rivals including OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta race to build AI agents that complete tasks on behalf of users. Google Labs acquired music generation platform ProducerAI earlier this year.

#5361. Zeno Power makes progress on an underwater power system that will eventually go nuclear

by Alan Boyle on Nov 19, 2026 at 7:00 amNovember 19, 2026 at 8:01 am

Zeno Power has hit a major milestone in its push to build nuclear batteries for underwater use.

The startup said today that it successfully demonstrated an electrically heated Stirling generator in a controlled maritime setting in Washington state. The two-week demonstration produced electrical power outputs in excess of 20 watts, said Lindsey Boles, Zeno’s chief product officer.

“It’s a really big step for us — just solidifying our expertise in how to design these, and then confirming our ability to translate that into operational hardware that meets or exceeds what our customers need,” Boles told GeekWire.

Zeno is developing the power system with support from the Department of Defense as a follow-up to an initial $7.5 million contract awarded in 2023. The generator uses a Stirling engine to convert heat into electricity by cycling gas through heating and cooling phases in a closed cylinder.

For the recent demonstration, the prototype device relied on an electric heating element. Future devices will instead rely on heat generated by the radioactive decay of strontium-90, a radioisotope that can be extracted from spent nuclear fuel.

Nuclear batteries have been in use for decades, primarily for space missions ranging from the Apollo moon shots to NASA’s Voyager spacecraft and Mars rovers. But the batteries being developed by Zeno Power promise to be at least four times more efficient than traditional radioisotope thermoelectric generators, Boles said.

Boles said the non-radiological test exceeded expectations. “There’s a difference between a design that works on paper and hardware that works in the field,” she said in a news release. “This is the moment our team has been building toward: proof that this technology works outside the lab.”

Long-lasting nuclear batteries could be used to power undersea sensor networks or recharge autonomous underwater vehicles. “There are a lot of applications, especially on the maritime front, that we really want electricity for,” Boles said. “And we really don’t need a ton of it. But we need it to be really reliable, and we need it to be long endurance, and we need it to be self-managed. … I think of it like a slow Tesla supercharger on the seabed.”

Retired Navy Adm. John Richardson, former chief of naval operations and a member of Zeno’s board of directors, called the recent test an “important step toward undersea superiority.”

“Protecting maritime infrastructure and powering distributed systems at sea requires energy; energy that lasts for years, not days or months,” Richardson said in a written statement. “As competition intensifies in contested domains, powered subsea systems will help keep us ahead. Zeno Power has steadily reduced risk, proven its technology, built a supply chain, and prepared to scale production.”

Next year, Zeno Power plans to install a radioisotope heat source in its generator and test the system in a water tank under controlled laboratory conditions. If those tests are successful, Zeno will move forward with the first operational seabed deployment of its radioisotope-fueled maritime system later in 2027.

The maritime battery isn’t Zeno’s only product. The company is also working on a nuclear-powered heater system for spacecraft, with a demonstration on the lunar surface planned as early as 2028. Zeno’s broader vision is to provide long-lasting, reliable power on the moon and Mars, and in extreme environments on Earth.

Since its founding in 2018, Zeno has secured $105 million in private capital and has brought in $60 million in contracts with the Pentagon and NASA. The company has more than 95 employees at locations in Seattle, California and Washington, D.C., with the largest contingent working at its engineering headquarters in Seattle’s South Lake Union district.

#5360. China Unicom Completes the World's First Standardized Live-Network Assessment of Autonomous Networks in the Core Network Domain, Advancing Industry Assessment Practices

BEIJING, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Recently, the new live network test standard TS1523B, Autonomous Network Level Test Specification for Core Network Fault Management, jointly developed by TM Forum and the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT), was released. The tests, which provide evidence aligned with TM Forum's Autonomous Network Level Assessment standards for core network fault management, were conducted for China Unicom by CAICT and subsequently validated independently by TM Forum. The specifications establish a unified framework for assessing autonomous capabilities in live networks.

During Innovate Asia, TM Forum and CAICT awarded the world's first commercial live network autonomy assessment in the core network domain. China Unicom, as the pioneering operator, successfully completed the end-to-end assessment, providing a reference for operators worldwide.

First Live-Network Testing Specifications Advance Autonomous Network Assessment

As autonomous networks evolve towards higher levels of autonomy, validating their performance in real-world environments is increasingly important. TM Forum has taken a leading role in advancing autonomous network assessment methodologies and standards, jointly developing and officially releasing the first set of live network testing specifications for core network fault management with CAICT. These specifications establish a unified framework for validating autonomous capabilities using real production network data. By analyzing operational data such as KPIs and operation logs, live network assessment provides observable, reproducible and traceable evidence. It complements self-assessment of Autonomous Network Levels using TM Forum's standardized tools by creating supporting evidence from real network environments. TM Forum recognizes the value of this approach and sees it as an important direction for further accelerating the deployment of higher-level autonomous capabilities. The release marks the first milestone in the strategic collaboration between TM Forum and CAICT in the Autonomous Networks domain.

China Unicom Validates Core Network Autonomy Following Live-Network Assessment

As the world's first operator to participate in a commercial live network AN Level assessment in the core network, China Unicom achieved a score of 3.8. The assessment focused on core network fault management and was conducted on China Unicom's network operations platform. Leveraging its Fault Management Center and Huawei's intelligent operations capabilities, China Unicom has established automated capabilities across awareness, analysis, decision and execution. Using actual production network data, the assessment team observed and analyzed the monthly number of successful 5GC diagnoses against the total number of diagnoses, verifying a diagnostic success rate of 98.3%. This demonstrates how live network assessment translates operational performance into measurable evidence, validating the effectiveness of autonomous capabilities in real networks. The assessment also provides valuable industry experience for applying reproducible, data-driven testing methods to autonomous networks. The test evidence and self-assessment results were subsequently validated by TM Forum's Autonomous Network Levels Assessment Validation service.

Going forward, TM Forum and industry partners will develop and promote live network testing for the assessment of AN levels for high-value scenarios, refining testing standards across network domains and use cases, helping accelerate higher-level autonomous networks and the intelligent transformation.

#5359. Amazon’s $18B bet on Anthropic tops $200B, for a moment, in the Claude maker’s historic market debut

by Todd Bishop on Nov 19, 2026 at 9:54 amNovember 19, 2026 at 10:10 am

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut today in a record $81.3 billion initial public offering, with big financial stakes for the Seattle area’s two tech giants.

For Amazon, the IPO is a paper windfall. The company started putting money into Anthropic in 2023, about $18 billion in all. At the $83 IPO price, its stake was worth about $161 billion. With Anthropic opening at $111.50 a share, that number was closer to $216 billion. The stock has since dropped below $100, which put Amazon’s stake under $200 billion.

Beyond the value of the investment, Anthropic is a major customer for Amazon’s cloud platform. The Claude maker has committed to spend at least $110 billion on Amazon Web Services through 2036.

For Microsoft, it’s more complicated. The Redmond company agreed in late 2025 to invest up to $5 billion but hasn’t disclosed the size of its stake. Microsoft is buying $1 billion of Anthropic stock alongside the IPO, one of seven tech companies buying a combined $26 billion. Anthropic has committed to spend at least $47 billion on Microsoft’s Azure cloud through 2033.

But Microsoft is also pitching its own AI models against Anthropic’s, and it has been working to replace Anthropic’s models with OpenAI’s in some Copilot features, The Information reported this week.

Listing Anthropic’s compute partners on CNBC this morning, co-founder Daniela Amodei named Nvidia, Amazon, Google and Broadcom, but not Microsoft. Whether it was a slip or something more significant, it was an interesting omission.

A historic debut: The offering tops SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO in June, and it makes Anthropic the first standalone AI lab to go public, ahead of OpenAI.

The five-year-old company was valued at about $1.5 trillion at the $83 IPO price, on a fully diluted basis that counts employee stock and other shares not yet issued. The stock opened at $111.50, valuing Anthropic at about $2 trillion on the same basis. It has since traded as low as about $95.

Speaking before the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei said Anthropic will slow the training and release of its AI models for as long as it takes to be confident they’re safe, and that going public only strengthens that resolve.

“We will not bend to either business nor political pressure,” he said.

In an interview with CNBC’s Andrew Ross Sorkin afterward, Amodei called the push and pull between growth and that kind of restraint “one of the central tensions at the heart of the company.”

Anthropic is also a public benefit corporation, a structure that legally requires the company to balance shareholders’ interests with the public good.

What’s next: Both Seattle-area giants have hedged their bets. Microsoft owns about 24% of OpenAI, and Amazon put $50 billion into OpenAI earlier this year.

OpenAI, which confidentially filed for its own IPO in June, is still aiming to go public in 2027.

Anthropic’s co-founders and some of its biggest shareholders are barred from selling for up to a year under the IPO’s lock-up rules, and Amazon has said it expects a customary lock-up period.

Amazon will update the value of its Anthropic holdings in its fourth-quarter results, much of it through earnings, which means the paper windfall is likely to boost Amazon’s fourth-quarter profit even though it hasn’t sold a share.

#5358. AIPro Supplies AI Video Analytics to Public Facilities and Power Plants, Expanding Site-Specific Safety Management

Fire monitoring at the KAMCO Human Resources Development Institute and person detection in the discharge zone at Goesan Hydropower Plant; on-device video analytics research also underway

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AIPro, an AI video analytics company, is expanding the use of its CCTV analytics technology to address site-specific safety challenges at public facilities and power plants. From software that detects signs of fires and wildfires to a system that detects people in a dam's downstream discharge zone, the company provides solutions tailored to each site's needs.

According to AIPro, the company has supplied fire and wildfire detection software to the Korea Asset Management Corporation (KAMCO) Human Resources Development Institute and VistaPro-FDS-002, a fire detection solution designated as an innovative product, to the Korea Gas Safety Corporation. At Goesan Hydropower Plant, operated by Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power, the company supplied a system that detects people in the dam's downstream discharge zone.

Each deployment uses CCTV video analytics for a distinct safety management objective. In fire monitoring, the focus is on detecting signs of fire, such as flames and smoke, in CCTV footage; in the discharge zone, the focus is on detecting the presence of people. The company explained that it tailors its video analytics capabilities to the monitoring requirements and operational objectives of each site.

VistaPro, the company's platform for enterprises and institutions, supports flame and smoke detection, people counting, and detection of people approaching or entering restricted areas, depending on the site configuration. AI-powered analysis helps managers assess on-site conditions and determine whether a response is needed. The platform is designed to reduce the workload of managers who must continuously monitor multiple CCTV feeds.

AIPro was founded in 2020 by Professor Chun-Su Park of Sungkyunkwan University. It translates research in computer vision and image processing into products that support safety management and operations at public facilities and industrial sites. The enterprise and institutional version of VistaPro has earned Grade 1 Good Software (GS) certification, and VistaPro-FDS-002 has been designated as an innovative product by the Public Procurement Service. The company's AI video analytics models have also undergone performance testing by the Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA).

The company's research and development efforts focus on improving both detection performance and operational efficiency. Building on its patented technology for improving the computational efficiency of video surveillance systems, the company continues to develop products that account for on-site imaging conditions and the computational load on hardware.

Through the "Super-Gap Startup 1000+" program, the company is currently developing an on-device software engine capable of running multiple deep learning models on devices deployed in the field. It is also conducting research on ultra-long-range object detection and low-power optimization. In addition, the company is participating in a project to develop and demonstrate an integrated AI-based system for early fire detection and suppression in livestock barns, gaining practical experience in field operations.

AIPro plans to draw on its experience deploying solutions at public institutions and conducting research and development to improve its products and expand adoption across sites of various sizes. By addressing site-specific needs such as fire monitoring, people counting, and restricted-area management, the company aims to help users in Korea and abroad adopt video analytics technology suited to their operational needs and scale.

#5357. Uncommon Thinkers: Andrew Redd’s audacious plan to turn ocean volcanoes into power plants

by Lisa Stiffler on Nov 19, 2026 at 10:07 amNovember 24, 2026 at 9:53 am

Editor’s note: This series profiles five Seattle-area “Uncommon Thinkers,” who will be recognized Dec. 10 at the GeekWire Gala in partnership with Greater Seattle Partners.

Andrew Redd‘s career path creates a tidy narrative: grow up in Seattle steeped in aviation and maritime culture, study mechanical engineering and aerospace, work at SpaceX, then launch an offshore geothermal energy startup.

The dots connect, but the picture they form is anything but ordinary: bold in vision, fast in execution and enormous in potential.

Redd has next-level ambition, and he’s directing it at solving one of the world’s biggest and most urgent problems — adding renewable, massively scalable energy that can outcompete fossil fuels and reach the grid quickly enough to make a difference in the race against climate change.

Underwater geothermal energy has never been tapped in a significant way, but to Redd, the idea was irresistible. “It checks all of the boxes for our perfect future energy source,” he said.

He founded Endurance Energy on the north shore of Seattle’s Lake Union in January 2025, and this September the team oversaw its fifth deep-sea deployment. At a site 300 miles off the Oregon coast, its prototype system generated more electricity than it consumed. The startup has raised $63 million from investors and has roughly three dozen employees.

Nate Bek, a principal at Ascend, praised Redd’s ability to attract “brilliant” talent in pursuit of his goal. The Seattle venture firm is one of the startup’s early backers.

“I’ve been deeply inspired by what [Redd]’s building at Endurance and haven’t shut up about it since the day we met,” Bek said. “He somehow makes powering the world from the bottom of the ocean feel inevitable, all while remaining remarkably measured and transparent about the progress.”

For Redd, studying engineering and aerospace in college was so clear-cut that it wasn’t a choice at all. Growing up around Boeing, seaplanes, the Museum of Flight and the Pacific Northwest’s rich maritime industry naturally pointed him toward those sectors. He wanted a degree as expansive as his influences.

“I didn’t really want to have to choose whether it was going to be boats or space travel or airplanes,” he said. “I just wanted to be able to do anything — keep the world as wide open as possible.”

After graduating from Princeton University, Redd worked at Neuralink, an Elon Musk company developing technology that lets the brain communicate directly with computers. A year later, in 2021, he moved to Musk’s rocket company, SpaceX.

That was another no-duh decision, as Redd viewed it.

“I saw SpaceX as really the place to be, where early-career people are given the most amount of resources and responsibility, and that felt like the fastest way to learn and the most engaging possible scenario to be in,” Redd said. “I wanted to be tossed into something that was a little bit crazy.”

Redd joined as SpaceX was starting to build its first orbital Starship rockets. The program brought together passionate young people and experienced SpaceX engineers who served as mentors. Wild ideas were entertained and explored. Everyone was committed to the mission. It was just the experience Redd wanted, and he planned to stick around for seven to 10 years.

Then artificial intelligence started booming.

In 2024, the build-out of sprawling, energy-hungry data centers for AI was accelerating with no end in sight. At the same time, efforts to electrify transportation, heating and cooling were driving up demand for power. Redd saw these trends sparking a surge in new natural gas generation, locking in decades of carbon emissions.

He wanted to find a better way. He went into engineering mode, focusing on all the essential criteria for an energy source: it had to be clean, not dependent on intermittent sun or wind, capable of producing massive amounts of energy, readily deployable, subject to fewer regulatory hurdles than something like nuclear, economically competitive, and scalable.

Redd recognized the tremendous heat contained under Earth’s surface as a terrific source for renewable energy and realized that most of the world’s active volcanoes are offshore. The unknown was whether the rocky ocean floor would be suitable for geothermal wells, so he did some research and found publications from geology experts who said the conditions would be “perfect.”

“You can tell,” he said, “when there’s a moment in time that you need to go and reach out and grab something, and that was really my impression — if I didn’t start this now, this would never come into existence, or wouldn’t come into existence soon enough to make a meaningful impact.”

In launching Endurance, Redd was intentional about the culture he wanted to create. He was aiming for a multidisciplinary group of mission-driven employees eager to collaborate and learn from each other: top talent that would attract more of the same and make Endurance a place people were excited to work.

“The hardest part of an early-stage startup is recruiting,” Redd said, “especially if you’re a first-time founder.”

The startup employs about a dozen SpaceX alumni, plus employees from the fusion company Helion Energy and the aerospace venture Blue Origin.

A strong team is key to Endurance’s success. That’s because, enthusiasm and passion aside, the startup faces steep engineering and economic challenges. The technology must withstand high pressure, corrosive conditions and mineral scaling inside devices, and seafloor machinery could be costly to repair. The systems will need expensive subsea cables to carry power to shore over potentially long distances. It’s a heavy lift.

While the September sea trial didn’t go perfectly, Redd is happy with the results. The company landed its 3-ton power plant on the seafloor near a natural vent and produced net energy from it — albeit for only 8.7 seconds. Technical difficulties and a power-cable failure cut the dive short.

Team members successfully operated the system remotely from Seattle through a fiber-optic network running along the seabed. Redd said he’s grateful for access to the network, which is part of the National Science Foundation’s Regional Cabled Array and operated by the University of Washington.

Endurance engineers also drilled what they called the world’s first subsea geothermal well at a site about 5,000 feet below the ocean’s surface. The 2-inch-wide, 52-foot-deep well delivered hydrothermal fluid, but the flow was too restricted to run the power plant, sending the team to the natural vent.

Redd said there’s a lot of work ahead, but the team “made huge strides” in learning and in reducing the project’s risks.

The company now is developing Leopard, its 2-megawatt generator. After testing the technology at the research site off the Oregon coast, Endurance aims to deliver power from a Leopard system in Tonga next year as its first commercial project. Subsea geothermal energy could ultimately reduce the island nation’s reliance on imported diesel and put the startup one step closer to its objective of generating terawatts of planet-friendly energy.

“This was always the end goal,” Redd said. “Create something that is highly meaningful for the world.”

Editor’s Note: Nate Bek of Ascend is a former GeekWire reporter.

#5356. Mercari Global App to Offer Mercari Japan Authentication and Auction Feature, Making it Easier Than Ever Before to Purchase Japanese Items From the US

Platform has surpassed 1 million cumulative registered usersâShipping discount promotion to be held in conjunction with Black Friday

TOKYO, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mercari, Inc. ("Mercari") has announced plans to begin offering Mercari Japan Authentication[1], a service that authenticates select items before they are shipped overseas from Japan, as well as an auction feature that will allow users in the US to bid on and purchase select auction items listed on the Japanese Mercari marketplace. Both Mercari Japan Authentication and the auction feature will be available through the Mercari Global App ("Global App"), a worldwide app that allows users to purchase items listed in Japan from overseas.

The cumulative number of registered users for the Global App surpassed 1 million[2] on August 28, 2026. As overseas usage expands, Mercari will create an environment where US users can have select items authenticated after purchase and before they are shipped overseas, allowing them to make purchases with peace of mind. By giving US users access to auctions, Mercari will also expand the number of opportunities for buyers to discover and purchase more Japanese items.

Additionally, in line with Black Friday and Cyber Monday in the US, Mercari will hold a promotion from November 24 to November 30, 2026, offering shipping discounts of up to 50 USD for select orders.

The Safe Appraisal service has been offered in Japan since March 2024.[3] Now, Mercari is starting to gradually offer the service for crossborder transactions for the US, allowing select items to be authenticated before they are shipped overseas. In the US, the name of the service is Mercari Japan Authentication. â

After a user purchases a trading card, pair of sneakers, fashion/luxury item, or another select item, it is sent to a designated authentication center in Japan, where expert staff verify the item according to category-specific authentication standards. Items that are found to satisfy the standards are shipped overseas. However, if an item does not satisfy the standards or cannot be authenticated, the transaction is canceled, and the buyer will be refunded for any expenses they paid such as the purchase price of the item, authentication fees, shipping costs, and taxes. Note that authentication does not guarantee the authenticity of the item. â

Once the item arrives at the authentication center, authentication typically takes three to five business days. This does not include the time required to ship the item. This is a system where the seller sets a starting price, prospective buyers place bids during the auction period, and the user who places the highest bid at the end wins the auction.

Mercari is now rolling out a feature in the Global App that allows users in the US to search for, view, bid on, win, and purchase select auction items listed on Mercari in Japan. In addition to fixed-price items, buyers will now be able to bid on and purchase select auction items as well.

Mercari will offer the fun of searching for, bidding on, and winning items such as trading cards and character merchandise to users in the US, while also expanding opportunities for sellers in Japan to deliver their items to users overseas.

Crossborder transactions on Mercari kicked off in 2019 with the start of partnerships with crossborder e-commerce operators. Following the launch of the web version of Mercari in Taiwan in August 2024, and in Hong Kong in May 2025, Mercari launched the Global App in Taiwan and Hong Kong in September 2025. The app launched in the US in June 2026.

With the Global App, users overseas can browse and buy Japanese items from Mercari and Mercari Shops. Mercari offers a platform where overseas users can purchase Japanese items by using translation features and support for payment methods in each country and region.

The gross merchandise value (GMV) of Mercari's crossborder business reached 112.2 billion JPY in the fiscal year ending June 2026, expanding approximately 19 times over the past four years.[5] â In addition, the cumulative number of registered users of the Global App surpassed 1 million on August 28, 2026.

For the period from April 2025 to March 2026, the US market ranked second in both transaction value and number of transactions for Mercari's crossborder business. Mercari launched the Global App in the US in June 2026, and by adding these latest two features, the company will further enhance the experience of purchasing Japanese items.

In November 2026, Mercari also made the decision to partner with SURUGA-YA Inc. to establish "Mercari Surugaya Inc.," a joint venture that will operate in the US. The joint venture plans to purchase, procure, and sell items in the Japanese Entertainment & Hobbies categories on the ground in the US.[6] Mercari will expand the touchpoints between US users and Japanese items through both the functional expansion of the Global App, which supports purchases of items from Japan, and local business operations in the US.

Mercari will hold a promotion on the Global App that discounts shipping costs for eligible orders by up to 50 USD. The promotion will coincide with Black Friday and Cyber Monday in the US.[7] During the promotion period, users who place an order totaling 50 USD or more will receive a discount on their shipping costs of up to 50 USD. The discount is automatically applied to eligible orders and can only be used once per user.

For details, see the promotional webpage.

Mercari will also hold a social media campaign called Golden ticket to Japan where users can check a code in a video posted on the mercari_global Instagram account and enter a draw via a promotional webpage.

#5355. So you got a Microsoft Voluntary Exit Offer? Here’s what to do next

by Nikesh Parekh on Nov 19, 2026 at 12:41 pmNovember 19, 2026 at 12:41 pm

Nikesh (Niki) Parekh is a former Microsoft GM who is now CEO of Seattle-based AI talent recruiting startup Provn. This is the fourth post in his series on “Life after Big Tech,” including the Seattle startup guide, laid off at 50 and VC funding is changing dramatically.

Tens of thousands of Microsoft employees have a big decision to make in the next few weeks: take the company’s offer to leave, or stay and take their chances.

Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the initiative in a memo on Oct. 26: a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) for about 60,000 employees at level 70 and below, which includes general managers and some vice presidents, in the U.S., Canada, the U.K. and India. That’s roughly 27% of Microsoft’s 223,000 people. The company expects 3,000 or fewer of them to accept.

Microsoft says the terms match its standard severance: base pay tied to level and tenure, continued stock vesting, a period of health coverage and career transition help. The severance package varies greatly based on the seniority or level of the employee and the number of years of service. Employees have until early December to decide and would leave by the end of the year.

The offer follows the Voluntary Retirement Program (VRP) that Microsoft extended to about 8,750 U.S. employees in April. About 30% of them, or roughly 2,600 people, took that offer.

All of this comes as Microsoft cuts jobs and changes the kinds of roles it hires for, while pouring money into AI infrastructure and data centers. At the same time, AI is reshaping the broader workforce, flattening management layers and changing what employers look for in new hires.

The worry I hear most is whether more layoffs are waiting on the other side. So the real choice is whether you leave on your own terms or let the company decide for you.

I hear two questions from Microsoft employees thinking about the VEO: How easily can I get another job, and how hard is it to start a company right now?

Harder than you think, and it depends a lot on who you are. We are in the “low hire, low fire” economy.

There is MASSIVE demand for AI-native builders — product managers, data scientists and engineers — as companies adapt products to deal with AI. Companies are also in the process of adopting AI.

One of the fastest-growing tech roles is the “Forward Deployed Engineer,” who implements AI solutions at customers. Security is also job #1 as models and agents get smarter and better at hacking legacy systems.

But it is very hard to be seen by recruiters and hiring managers right now. Candidates are using AI to customize their resumes to each job and using AI agents to apply, sending out 100 to 200 job applications per day. Recruiters are inundated with resumes and job applications, many of which are fake or inappropriate for the role.

It is critical to leverage your network in the job search, which can be hard if you have spent your entire career within one company.

“It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a company.”

Hiring managers have changed what they look for, too. AI fluency is becoming table stakes. The “process” of how you build/sell/market with AI is more important than what you build. Candidates are expected to show prototypes and proof of how they use AI tools every day.

The jobs themselves are changing. A friend told me last month that he wanted an engineering manager role. There are fewer manager roles in the market now.

AI has driven a reduction in management layers and a general flattening of organizations. The engineering team at a small AI company today is a CTO and a group of strong individual contributors. It is normal for managers to have 10 to 30 direct reports now, versus five to 10 in the pre-AI era.

Product management, program management and design teams are shrinking, as well, as AI automates certain jobs.

Hiring managers may view spending your whole career at Microsoft as a yellow flag. Microsoft is an iconic but unusual company. Almost no one else sells to and services customers the way Microsoft does, with an account executive inside nearly every large enterprise in the world.

The skills that get you promoted in Redmond don’t always carry over to a 500- to 5,000-person software company.

It has never been easier to build a product, and it has rarely been harder to fund a company.

Software is cheap to build now. A product leader and an engineer using AI tools can ship in weeks what used to take a team a year.

This cuts both ways for startups. Every good idea attracts a dozen competitors within months, and the big platforms will copy anything that works.

The true strength of a startup today is the ability to grow revenue quickly and establish leadership in a beachhead market. The sales, marketing, product-led growth and distribution strategies are becoming the most critical parts of the business.

The bar for venture funding is extremely high. Jason Lemkin of SaaStr recently shared data from ICONIQ showing that top “AI forward” startups under $10 million in annual recurring revenue are growing 900% a year at the median.

One venture investor told me they advise their portfolio companies that if they aren’t on track for a $10 million run rate within two years, they won’t raise another round. Last week I spoke with an investor who owns part of a business with $4 million in revenue, growing 100% a year and losing $1 million, and it can’t raise.

1) Think VERY big, raise a lot and grow fast enough to justify it. Build an incredible team pursuing an ambitious idea. Raise a large round based on the promise of becoming the next Anthropic, OpenAI or legal AI startup Harvey. Many of the most interesting companies are not software or AI-related, but are “deep tech” companies in defense, robotics, energy and biotech.

2) Raise a moderate amount of money from angels, family offices and nontraditional funds to build a business that has the ability to be profitable on one round of financing. You can control your destiny by building a company that doesn’t rely on the venture capital funding market.

3) Bootstrap and build a business that you own. Fund it yourself, grow it with revenue and get to profitability.

The question that most people are NOT asking is: What do I really want?

Before December, block out an afternoon and think about the last time you were happy at work.

There are many frameworks for figuring out what you want in your career and life in general. I’m a fan of the Four Elements exercise. Write down three times in your career when you felt energized and effective. From those, work out what gives you energy, where you have the most impact, what culture you do best in and what your constraints are: money, kids, aging parents and how many more years you want to work.

On LinkedIn, I have seen examples of Microsoft employees taking the VEO to start their own businesses in property management, buy car washes, take time to recharge, spend time with family and travel.

Other employees are starting the job search in earnest but not taking the VEO. Many others are just getting back to work and doubling down on Microsoft.

Whichever way you go, start now. Start by aligning on your priorities and what you want from your career. If you stay, use the next year to build your skills with AI and to grow a network outside Redmond. If you leave to build something, decide early which of the three funding paths you’re on, because that choice shapes everything that follows.

The people I’ve watched land well after Big Tech had one thing in common: they knew what they wanted before they walked out the door, whether that was a new role, a company of their own or a year with their family.

MediaTek powers more than two billion devices every year, from the most advanced AI infrastructure on the planet to the everyday devices that make life smarter, faster, and more connected. For everyone. MediaTek silicon is the common thread running through all of it. Yeah, MediaTek does that.

#5354. Crypto News Today: Is Bitcoin Bottoming Out? BTC Bounces Back After PCE Shock

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Bitcoin bounced back toward $60,000 this morning after news on hotter-than-expected US inflation broke and sent the crypto tumbling to $57,300, its lowest level in more than two years. The rebound has brought back speculation that Bitcoin may finally be approaching a bottom, but ETF outflows and bearish signals continue to cloud the outlook.

October’s Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation came in at 3.8% annually, while core PCE reached 3.3%, above the 3.2% expected by economists. These figures strengthened concerns that the Federal Reserve could keep monetary policy restrictive for longer, which then adds pressure to risk assets like Bitcoin.

Bitcoin nevertheless recovered after briefly dipping below $58,000, as we gauge and predict its next move.

Bitcoin remains down 23% this November, putting it on track for its worst monthly performance since June 2022. Spot Bitcoin ETFs have also suffered nearly $5 billion in net outflows this month through November 24, adding another source of selling pressure.

BlackRock’s IBIT has accounted for more than $4 billion in redemptions during the month, showing how quickly institutional demand has reversed.

However, not all investors are moving in the same direction. Data cited by Nansen shows wallets that rarely move Bitcoin received a net 10,000 BTC from exchanges over the past month, while ETFs collectively sold 70,000 BTC during November.

Nansen data shows large, infrequently moving wallets absorbed a net 10,000 BTC from exchanges over the past month.Meanwhile, spot Bitcoin ETFs sold 70,000 BTC in November.The imbalance is stark. Long term cold wallets are still accumulating, but nowhere near enough to offset…

Bitcoin’s rebound also comes after an arguably huge derivatives-market reset, with leveraged positions being flushed out during the recent slide. That could reduce some immediate selling pressure.

Holders have realized $8.4 billion in net losses over the past 30 days, according to CryptoQuant data, as investors are increasingly capitulating during the selloff. But the figure remains well below the $30 billion recorded during February’s bottom and $18.4 billion during June’s low. Selling pressure has intensified, but the scale of realized losses has yet to match previous capitulation events.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Some analysts believe Bitcoin’s recovery could be running ahead of the underlying market conditions. CoinMarketCap research head Alice Liu warned that the rebound may largely reflect short sellers covering positions, and not fresh demand, leaving prices vulnerable once that buying subsides.

Meanwhile, 10x Research’s bearish signal issued in October correctly anticipated Bitcoin’s decline toward $57,300. The firm has cautioned that oversold conditions can trigger short-term rebounds without necessarily signaling a reversal in the wider trend.

“Bitcoin has reached our $57,300 target. Short-term indicators were oversold for much of the decline, and tactical bounces were always possible. Our market structure work, however, kept pointing to a bearish primary trend.” – 10X Research

Bitcoin faces a difficult combination of persistent ETF withdrawals, uncertain news from Federal Reserve policy, and weakened market sentiment. The selloff has removed substantial leverage, but convincing evidence of renewed demand remains limited.

The $57,300 low is now a key level to defend. Holding that support while ETF outflows begin slowing will likely strengthen the case that Bitcoin is forming a bottom.
